subject: Unexpected throttles observed — action plan and post-incident follow-up
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@acme-health.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-12T15:15:00Z
Subject: Unexplained 429 surge since yesterday afternoon

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing a spike in 429 responses from Redwood starting yesterday (~16:00 PST). About 25-35% of our /generate calls are getting throttled — it's affecting our app's user experience. We've attached a short sample of errors and timestamps.

Quick details:
- Environment: prod-us-west1
- Model: gpt-large-v1 (stable)
- Approx call volume: ~8k/min during peak windows
- First seen: 2025-09-11 16:05 PDT

Can you confirm if there was any policy change or rollout on your side? We need to know whether to pause any jobs on our end.

Attachments: api-trace-logs-0912.txt (snippet)

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Lead SRE, Acme Health
apiops@acme-health.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-13T09:40:00Z
Subject: Acme Health 429s — early root cause hypothesis and remediation steps

Team — quick summary of what I pulled together after looking at the traces and our rollout timeline. TL;DR: a rate-limit shaping policy that we rolled as part of regional SLO enforcement accidentally included a legacy org filter that matched Acme's org id pattern, applying a more aggressive token refill rate than intended.

Evidence:
- Policy rollout: 2025-09-11 14:22Z to us-west1 (canary -> global).
- Policy diff shows an extra predicate that catches org ids starting with "acme-" (see attached).
- Gateway traces show immediate refill mismatches and burst deficits at 2025-09-11 16:03Z (first customer errors align).

Immediate remediation executed (13:05Z):
- Rolled back the suspect policy from us-west1 canary pool. (completed)
- Applied a temporary +30% quota to Acme Health for next 72 hours while we monitor.
- Opened INC-8741 to track full postmortem and billing/credit assessment.

Follow-ups required:
1) Produce incident timeline and share with customer (Hannah, can you draft?).
2) Engineering: add unit test to policy diff deploys to prevent predicate bleed. (Marcus)
3) CS/Finance: prepare a goodwill credit proposal (Vanessa).

Attachment: policy-diff.patch

— Vanessa

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@acme-health.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-13T12:10:00Z
Subject: Update — mitigation applied and monitoring in place

Hi Lena,

Update from our side: we've completed a rollback of the rate-limit shaping policy that looked to be the cause. We also issued a temporary +30% quota increase for Acme Health for 72 hours as an immediate mitigation.

What to expect now:
- You should see the 429s drop to baseline within the next 10–20 minutes (most customers recovered within 5–10).
- We've enabled a dedicated alert for your org id so we get immediate paging if there's any regression.
- We'll send a full incident timeline and a proposed credit/compensation package by EOD tomorrow.

Can you confirm whether your traffic has normalized on your end? If you still see throttles, please include a few request ids and timestamps so I can correlate.

Attachments: incident-timeline-0913.csv

Thanks for your patience — we're treating this as high priority.

— Vanessa

From: Lena Ortiz <lena@acme-health.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-13T13:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Update — mitigation applied and monitoring in place

Vanessa — thanks for the quick response and the temporary quota bump. Traffic has largely returned to normal; we saw a brief tail of errors but it's within acceptable bounds now.

A couple of follow-ups from our side:
- Can you confirm the affected window (start/end) so we can reconcile against our SLAs?
- We'll likely request a goodwill credit for the impacted hours; please route this through your billing/finance.

I'll hold on further action until I see the incident timeline. Appreciate the quick triage.

— Lena
Lead SRE, Acme Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finance Team <finance@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-15T17:32:00Z
Subject: Postmortem follow-up & customer remediation plan (Acme Health)

Team — finalizing follow-ups from the Acme Health incident (INC-8741). Summary and proposed customer remediation below.

Incident summary (brief):
- Root cause: rollout of a rate-limit shaping policy with an overly-broad predicate matched Acme org ids, leading to unexpected token refill behavior and increased 429s.
- Impact window: 2025-09-11T16:03:00Z -> 2025-09-13T12:05:00Z (policy rollback completed 2025-09-13T12:05:00Z).
- Affected customers: Acme Health (primary reported), internal metrics show similar small blips for two other orgs; we are contacting those customers separately.

Proposed remediation for Acme Health:
1) Goodwill credit: 10% credit applied to September invoiced usage for the impacted window. (Finance to approve/execute)
2) Permanent: increase default quota floor for Acme by 20% and add a dedicated alert/automation that auto-rolls back policy changes impacting their org id pattern.
3) Engineering actions: add deploy-time predicate validation tests and a pre-deploy canary checker to prevent predicate bleed; ETA: 2025-10-03. (Owner: Marcus)
4) Customer comms: send finalized postmortem doc and a short documentation note describing the change control steps we've added. (Owner: Hannah)

Attachments: postmortem-0915-draft.pdf
Related: JIRA INC-8741, Drive folder with raw traces: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_drive_link

Requests:
- Finance: confirm and action the goodwill credit (please update INC-8741).
- Marcus: confirm ETA for the deploy-time test and the canary checker.
- Hannah: finalize the postmortem doc and the customer-facing note; I'll coordinate the delivery with Acme.

Thanks — Vanessa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
